entries.text: SCENE: The Great Hall at Monkswell Manor. Late afternoon. The home looks not so much a period piece but a house which has been lived in by generations of the same family with dwindling resources. There are tall windows up Centre; a big arched opening up Right leading to the entrance hall, the front door and the kitchen; and an arched opening Left leading upstairs to the bedrooms. Up Left leading off the stairs is the door to the library; down Left is the door to the drawing room; and down Right the door (opening on stage) to the dining room. Right is an open fireplace, and beneath the window up Centre a windowseat and a radiator. The hall is furnished as a lounge. There is some good old oak, including a large refectory table by the window up Centre, an oak chest in the entrance hall up Right, and a stool on the stairs Left. The curtains and the upholstered furniture ― a sofa Left Centre, an armchair Centre, a large leather armchair Right, and a small Victorian armchair down Right ― are shabby and old-fashioned. There is a combined desk and bookcase Left, with a radio and telephone on it and a chair beside it. There is another chair up Right Centre by the window, a Canterbury containing newspapers and magazines above the fireplace and a small half-circular card table behind the sofa. There are two wall brackets over the fireplace which are worked together; and a wall bracket on the Left wall, one Left of the library door and one in the entrance hall, which are also worked together. There are double switches Left of the arch up Right, and on the downstage side of the door down Left, and a single switch on the upstage side of the door down Right. A table lamp stands on the sofa table.
entries.summaryJa: 場面：モンクスウェル・マナーの大広間。午後遅く。この家は時代物の展示品というより、資産が次第に乏しくなってきた同じ一族が何世代にもわたって住み続けてきた家に見える。舞台奥中央に高い窓があり、舞台奥右の大きなアーチ状の開口部は玄関ホール、玄関のドア、台所へ通じる。左のアーチ状の開口部は寝室へ上がる階段につながる。階段から続く舞台奥左に図書室のドア、舞台手前左に応接間のドア、舞台手前右に食堂のドアがある。舞台右には暖炉があり、奥中央の窓の下には窓際の腰掛けとラジエーターがある。ホールはラウンジとして整えられ、古い良質なオーク家具が置かれている。奥中央の窓際に大きな食堂用テーブル、奥右の玄関ホールにオーク材の大型収納箱、左の階段に腰掛けがある。カーテンや布張りの家具は古びて時代遅れで、左中央にソファ、中央に肘掛け椅子、右に大きな革張りの肘掛け椅子、手前右に小さなヴィクトリア朝風の肘掛け椅子がある。左には机と本棚が一体になった家具があり、その上にラジオと電話、そばに椅子がある。奥右中央の窓際にも椅子があり、暖炉の上には新聞や雑誌を入れたカンタベリー、ソファの後ろには半円形の小さなカードテーブルがある。暖炉上の二つの壁付け照明は連動し、左壁・図書室のドア左・玄関ホール側の壁付け照明も連動する。舞台奥右のアーチ左、手前左のドアの舞台手前側には二連スイッチがあり、手前右のドアの舞台奥側には単独スイッチがある。ソファテーブルにはテーブルランプが置かれている。

entries.text: Before Curtain rises the House LIGHTS fade to a complete blackout and the music of "Three Blind Mice" is heard. When Curtain rises the stage is in complete darkness. The music fades, giving place to a shrill whistle of the same tune, "Three Blind Mice." A woman's piercing scream is heard, then a mixture of male and female voices saying: "My God, what's that?" "Went that way!" "Oh, my God!" Then a police ― whistle sounds, followed by several other police whistles, all of which fade to silence.
entries.summaryJa: 幕が上がる前に客席照明が完全な暗転まで落ち、「Three Blind Mice」の音楽が聞こえる。幕が上がっても舞台は真っ暗なまま。音楽が弱まり、同じ曲を吹く鋭い口笛に変わる。女性の甲高い悲鳴が聞こえ、続いて男女の声が入り交じって叫ぶ。その後、警察の笛が鳴り、さらに複数の警察笛が続き、すべての音が次第に消えて静寂になる。

entries.text: The LIGHTS come up, revealing the Hall at Monkswell Manor. It is late afternoon, and almost dark. Snow can be seen falling heavily through the windows up Centre. There is a fire burning. A freshly painted signboard is standing on its side on the stairs against the archway Left; it has on it in large letters: MONKWELL MANOR GUEST HOUSE.
entries.summaryJa: 照明が上がり、モンクスウェル・マナーのホールが見える。時刻は午後遅く、もうほとんど暗い。舞台奥中央の窓の外には雪が激しく降っている。暖炉には火が燃えている。塗りたての看板が左のアーチ脇の階段に横倒しに立てかけられ、「MONKWELL MANOR GUEST HOUSE」と大きく書かれている。

entries.text: SCENE: The same. The following afternoon. When Curtain rises it is not snowing, but snow can be seen banked high against the window. MAJOR METCALF is seated on the sofa reading a book, and MRS. BOYLE is sitting in the large armchair Right in front of the fire, writing on a pad on her knee.
entries.summaryJa: 場面は同じ大広間。翌日の午後。幕が上がると雪は降っていないが、窓の外には雪が高く積もっている。MAJOR METCALFはソファに座って本を読み、MRS. BOYLEは暖炉前の舞台右にある大きな肘掛け椅子に座り、膝の上のメモ用紙に何かを書いている。

entries.text: SCENE: The same. Ten minutes later. When the Curtain rises, MRS. BOYLE's body has been removed and EVERYONE is assembled in the room. TROTTER is in charge and is sitting on the up stage side of the refectory table. MOLLIE is standing at the Right end of the refectory table. The others are all sitting, MAJOR METCALF in the large armchair Right, CHRISTOPHER in the dark chair, GILES on the stairs Left, MISS CASEWELL at the Right end of the sofa, and PARAVICINI at the Left end.
entries.summaryJa: 場面は同じ大広間。10分後。幕が上がるとMRS. BOYLEの遺体はすでに運び出され、全員が部屋に集まっている。TROTTERが場を仕切り、長い食堂用テーブルの舞台奥側に座っている。MOLLIEはそのテーブルの右端に立っている。ほかの人物は全員座っており、MAJOR METCALFは舞台右の大きな肘掛け椅子、CHRISTOPHERは濃色の椅子、GILESは舞台左の階段、MISS CASEWELLはソファ右端、PARAVICINIはソファ左端にいる。

He stamps his feet to shake off the snow, opens the oak chest and puts inside a big paper carrier he has been carrying. He takes off his overcoat, hat and scarf, moves down and throws them on the armchair Centre. Then he goes to the fire and warms his hands.
